title: quant-kernel: improve INT8/FP8 smoothquant + dequant-fusion paths, KV-cache scheduling and continuous batching
author: Alex Chen
release_notes: Performance: ~1.6x average throughput improvement for INT8/FP8 quantized models on A100 across mixed-length workloads; improved tail latency under heavy KV-cache pressure. Backwards compatible: runtime falls back to previous dequant path when fusion not applicable.
description:
Motivation: reduce per-token cost and improve latency for quantized inference (INT8/FP8) by (1) fully adapting smoothquant flow into the fused dequant path, (2) improving kernel scheduling when KV-cache misses/evictions happen, and (3) integrating continuous batching heuristics to pick fusion-friendly batch boundaries. This PR bundles a set of coordinated changes across the serving runtime, kernels, and scheduler.

Changes: 
- Kernel: add fused smoothquant->dequant->matmul kernel for INT8/FP8 codepath, including specialized FP8 accumulation and re-scaling microkernels. The fused kernel avoids an extra dequant/transpose step for many attention configurations.
- KV cache/scheduler: introduce a short-circuit path that prioritizes fused-kernel capable shards when a request touches a cached prefix and the shard is fusion-capable; improves locality and reduces stale-cache stalls.
- Continuous batching: update the batching policy to prefer batch cut points aligned to token boundaries that maximize fusion utilization; add a small online estimator to trade throughput vs. tail latency.
- Fallbacks: runtime detects capability at model-load time and falls back to the de-fused path for incompatible models or hardware. Added runtime flag `--enable-quant-fusion` (default: true) for operators and per-model opt-out.
- Tests & benchmarks: microbenchmarks, system-level load tests, and updated integration tests covering warm/cold KV-cache and mixed-length chat workloads.

Benchmark highlights (internal test cluster, A100-80GB):
- Chat workload (median sequence 128, max 2048) with mix of 40% short/60% long inputs: throughput +60% and median p95 tail latency -18% for INT8 profiles.
- Encoder-decoder style eval: stable ~1.6x throughput for FP8 quantized variants vs previous dequant path.
- KV-cache heavy scenario (many prefix hits): tail latency improved by 25% and overall request success under load increased.

Compatibility & risks:
- FP8 accumulation uses updated reprojection scalers; we validated with float32 reference but recommend running customer QA for task-specific regressions.
- Fusion introduces a new codepath that touches low-level kernels; added an incremental rollout (canary) and an opt-out per-model at runtime.

References: Linear ENG-4821, previous PRs around quant kernels and smoothquant (see linked PRs in repo).

review_conversation: Priya Nair: Please add a fallback when FP8 accumulation overflows; what limits do we set?

Diego Alvarez: Kernel looks good, but microkernel performance varies with seq_len=1. Can we special-case single-token paths?
Alex Chen: Added a fast-path for seq_len=1 that avoids packing/unpacking and regresses nothing on longer sequences.
Samir Patel: CI flake on linux-gcc-9 was unrelated; ran full perf bench and results look solid. Approving pending doc tweaks.

notes: Canary rollout executed on 10% of serving capacity for 48 hours; no regressions observed in customer telemetries. Ops scheduled a gradual ramp to 50% over the next week. Monitoring: p95 latency and token/sec per model. If issues observed, runtime flag --enable-quant-fusion=false can be set per-model.
known_issues: Edgecase: some older CUDA drivers show minor FP8 accumulation jitter; driver upgrade recommended.
Perf: tiny throughput regressions for single-GPU small-batch (<4) on T4; fallback enabled by default for those configs.
